Stronger cooperation between China and Europe is important for the future of global health governance, particularly in areas such as artificial intelligence, primary health care and healthy aging, said Hans Kluge, Belgium's nominee for director-general of the World Health Organization (WHO) and WHO regional director for Europe on special leave.

Promoting healthy aging also requires a shift toward prevention, with health interventions starting early in life, Kluge said in an exclusive interview with CGTN's Health Talk on the sidelines of the Boao Forum for Asia Global Health Forum.

He stressed the importance of collaboration between the health and education sectors and of maintaining healthy lifestyles, particularly through regular physical activity.

The Boao Forum for Asia Global Health Forum 2026 was held in Haikou from September 15 to 16. Guests from 32 countries and regions attended the event.

recentItems.title: Roots in Jingdezhen: An American artist 3D prints a forgotten technique
recentItems.description:
When 3D printing meets the 1,000-year-old kiln fires of Jingdezhen, creative sparks fly. The city in east China's Jiangxi Province has made porcelain for a millennium and is known as China's porcelain capital.

American artist Michael May, from Oklahoma, set up his studio there and is now pursuing a PhD at the city's ceramic university. He blends 3D printing with the ancient craft Jingdezhen is famous for.

"I'm doing something nobody has done before," he says. "Sometimes it's lonely."

He's watched friends and classmates give up along the way, which is why he pushes his students to stay the course. As for himself, he's given up a lot to be here. Quitting wasn't on the table.

In Jingdezhen, he explores the history and feels the city's tradition, openness and warmth. The film is about what keeps him there: the quiet workbench he found in the countryside, among rice fields and hills, a cup of tea from a local and the joy in children's faces as they make pottery from mud. #coolchina

recentItems.title: World-first treatment corrects giant panda's jaw asymmetry
recentItems.description:
Experts from West China Hospital of Stomatology, Sichuan University, and the Chengdu Research Base of Giant Panda Breeding have completed what they describe as the world's first functional orthopedic treatment for mandibular asymmetry in a giant panda.

Using intraoral scans and 3D digital technology, the team designed a custom appliance for four-year-old Beixia, whose jaw had shifted left after injuries sustained shortly after birth. After six months of treatment, Beixia's jaw was largely corrected and his sucking, chewing and swallowing functions returned to normal.

recentItems.title: National Teeth-care Day: Expert tips on daily oral care and misconceptions
recentItems.description:
To mark the 38th National Teeth-care Day, Professor Hu Wenjie, vice dean of the Peking University School and Hospital of Stomatology, addresses common oral health misconceptions. He explains why sugar-free drinks can still erode enamel, why teeth that feel healthy might still need attention, and why early prevention is essential for lifelong oral health.

recentItems.title: Ex-PM of Kyrgyzstan says each country needs to develop in its own way
recentItems.description:
Every country in the world is different, and there is no universal blueprint for development and reform, says Djoomart Kaipovich Otorbaev, former prime minister of Kyrgyzstan. According to him, one-size-fits-all solutions will not work for all nations, and practical approaches based on individual national realities are necessary.
